brief.problem: Customers and operations need a clear, traceable payment journey, including held instructions and uncertain settlement outcomes.
brief.goal: Define the responsibilities needed to move a domestic payment from instruction to a known outcome.
brief.source: Illustrative reference brief — confirm against your project

artefacts.title: A payment with a known outcome
artefacts.description: Customers can follow an instruction to a confirmed, held, or pending outcome.

artefacts.title: Protect the financial effect
artefacts.description: An instruction must not cause an unintended duplicate debit.

artefacts.title: Payments product owner
artefacts.description: Accountable for the payment experience and the scope of the service.

artefacts.title: Payment operations lead
artefacts.description: Accountable for held payments, uncertain outcomes, and operational follow-up.

artefacts.title: Bank customer
artefacts.description: Submits an instruction and needs to understand its current outcome.

artefacts.title: Operations analyst
artefacts.description: Investigates held instructions and uncertain settlement outcomes.

artefacts.title: Domestic account-to-account payment
artefacts.description: In scope: instruction capture, risk screening, posting, settlement, and outcome enquiry.

artefacts.title: Card and international payments
artefacts.description: Out of scope for this reference journey.

artefacts.title: Initiate payment
artefacts.description: The customer submits an instruction with a destination, amount, and request reference.

artefacts.title: Screen the instruction
artefacts.description: Screen the instruction and choose whether to allow or hold it.

artefacts.title: Record the posting
artefacts.description: Record the authorised financial effect with the existing request reference.

artefacts.title: Settle the payment
artefacts.description: Submit the external leg and track a confirmed or uncertain response.

artefacts.title: Communicate the outcome
artefacts.description: Expose the known status and the next action to the customer or operations.

artefacts.title: Use the existing core ledger
artefacts.description: The reference project assumes the current ledger remains the book of record. Confirm with the bank.

artefacts.title: Settlement status can be enquired
artefacts.description: An enquiry can resolve an uncertain external response. Contract evidence is still required.

artefacts.title: Accept a traceable payment instruction
artefacts.description: The service shall accept a valid instruction and return a stable request reference.
artefacts.acceptance: Given a valid instruction, when it is accepted, then a request reference is returned and can be used for status enquiry.

artefacts.title: Hold an instruction that needs review
artefacts.description: The service shall hold an instruction that requires additional screening and expose its reason.
artefacts.acceptance: Given an instruction that requires review, when screening completes, then its status is held and no ledger posting occurs.

artefacts.title: Prevent duplicate financial effects
artefacts.description: The service shall recognise a repeated instruction reference and preserve one financial effect.
artefacts.acceptance: Given an instruction already posted, when the same reference is retried, then the recorded outcome is returned without another debit.

artefacts.title: Retain an uncertain settlement outcome
artefacts.description: The service shall keep an uncertain response pending until an enquiry resolves it.
artefacts.acceptance: Given no definitive settlement response, when the request times out, then the outcome remains pending and the same reference is retained for enquiry.

artefacts.title: Notify the customer quickly
artefacts.description: The service shall notify the customer quickly after the payment outcome is known.

drivers.title: Preserve one financial effect
drivers.stimulus: A posted instruction is retried with the same reference.
drivers.conditions: A timeout or client retry occurs after a posting may already have succeeded.
drivers.response: Return the recorded outcome and prevent an additional debit.
drivers.measurement: Reconcile the ledger postings against the original instruction reference.
drivers.rationale: An unintended duplicate debit changes the customer’s balance.
drivers.tactic: Atomic duplicate detection and a durable result record.
drivers.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey scenario — confirm with stakeholders

drivers.title: Keep instruction intake available
drivers.stimulus: A customer submits a valid instruction during a component outage.
drivers.conditions: During the agreed service window; dependency and maintenance exclusions need agreement.
drivers.response: Accept the instruction or return an explicit unavailable response without losing its reference.
drivers.measurement: Measure eligible successful intake probes against all eligible probes. Agree exclusions.
drivers.rationale: Customers need a dependable entry point; the service window must be agreed.
drivers.tactic: Health checks and bounded failover with explicit degraded behaviour.
drivers.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey scenario — confirm with stakeholders

drivers.title: Acknowledge a payment predictably
drivers.stimulus: A customer submits a valid payment instruction.
drivers.conditions: At representative peak load with screening dependencies available.
drivers.response: Return the accepted reference or an explicit hold response. This measures acknowledgement, not final settlement.
drivers.window: Across the agreed peak-load test window
drivers.measurement: Measure from receipt of an instruction to acknowledgement; record load and percentile.
drivers.rationale: A slow acknowledgement encourages repeat submissions and support enquiries.
drivers.tactic: Bounded timeouts and workload isolation; keep integrity checks in the path.
drivers.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey scenario — confirm with stakeholders

drivers.title: Resolve uncertainty without unsafe retries
drivers.stimulus: The external settlement request times out without a definitive response.
drivers.conditions: The original reference and posting record remain available.
drivers.response: Keep the payment pending, enquire about its status, and assign unresolved cases for investigation.
drivers.metric: Time until an uncertain payment is investigated
drivers.window: From the first uncertain response for each affected instruction
drivers.measurement: Compare the uncertain-response timestamp with an enquiry result or an assigned investigation record.
drivers.rationale: A blind retry could duplicate the financial effect or misstate the outcome.
drivers.tactic: Durable pending state, status enquiry, and reconciliation before retry.
drivers.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey scenario — confirm with stakeholders

drivers.title: Reject an unauthorised instruction
drivers.stimulus: An unauthorised actor attempts to submit or inspect a payment.
drivers.conditions: The actor lacks the required identity, entitlement, or access to the payment.
drivers.response: Reject the operation and record the attempted access without exposing payment details.
drivers.window: Across the agreed negative-access test cases
drivers.measurement: Test missing, expired, and insufficient entitlements and verify denial and audit evidence.
drivers.rationale: The actor must be entitled to the instruction and its information.
drivers.tactic: Server-side authorisation at each trust boundary with auditable denial.
drivers.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey scenario — confirm with stakeholders

drivers.title: Retain the payment trail across boundaries
drivers.stimulus: A customer or analyst investigates an instruction’s current outcome.
drivers.conditions: The payment spans screening, posting, settlement, and notification responsibilities.
drivers.response: Retrieve correlated events and the recorded outcome using the original reference.
drivers.metric: Required journey stages carrying the original reference
drivers.window: For each sampled instruction across the required stages
drivers.measurement: Correlate the recorded events and verify that each required stage retains the reference.
drivers.rationale: Operations need to explain a payment’s history and locate an uncertain outcome.
drivers.tactic: Propagate correlation references and retain an access-controlled event trail.
drivers.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey scenario — confirm with stakeholders

records.question: When should the customer receive a payment acknowledgement?
records.context: Separate acceptance of an instruction from final settlement. Compare response time, durable handoff, and operational complexity.
records.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey decision question
records.assumptions: The customer channel can display a pending payment and retrieve its later outcome.
records.risks: A queued instruction may be acknowledged before settlement finishes.

alternatives.title: Keep the customer request synchronous
alternatives.summary: Keep the request open through the required downstream work and return the recorded result.
alternatives.benefits: A direct request/response path with fewer moving parts.
alternatives.costs: Dependency latency and outages reach the customer request. A timeout can leave an uncertain result.
alternatives.consequences: Payment API owns a bounded wait and must distinguish rejection from an unknown outcome.
alternatives.antiPattern: Treating an HTTP timeout as proof that the payment failed.

relationships.label: Wait for a bounded settlement response

alternatives.title: Acknowledge a durable asynchronous handoff
alternatives.summary: Persist the instruction, acknowledge acceptance, and complete settlement independently.
alternatives.benefits: Decouples acknowledgement from downstream settlement duration.
alternatives.costs: Adds pending-state handling, durable delivery, reconciliation, and operational ownership.
alternatives.consequences: Payment API acknowledges acceptance. Settlement hub owns completion; notification reports the verified outcome.
alternatives.antiPattern: Fire-and-forget delivery or claiming that acceptance means settlement.

records.question: Where should one financial effect be enforced?
records.context: A timeout, network retry, or repeated instruction must be evaluated at the authoritative posting boundary.
records.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey decision question
records.assumptions: The authoritative posting boundary can associate a unique instruction reference with its result.
records.risks: A check separate from the posting transaction can race with another request.

alternatives.title: Enforce the reference at the posting boundary
alternatives.summary: Bind duplicate detection and result lookup to the authoritative posting operation.
alternatives.benefits: Retains the original result across process restarts and repeated requests.
alternatives.costs: Requires agreement on reference uniqueness, retention, and transactional behaviour.
alternatives.consequences: Core ledger owns the one-effect guarantee; Payment API reuses the original reference.
alternatives.antiPattern: Assuming idempotency without checking concurrent requests and failure boundaries.

alternatives.title: Suppress repeats in the application cache
alternatives.summary: Use a short-lived application record to reduce repeated submissions.
alternatives.benefits: Can reduce repeated work near the channel.
alternatives.costs: A restart, expiry, or concurrent request can bypass the guard.
alternatives.consequences: This is an optimisation; on its own it does not establish a durable financial guarantee.
alternatives.antiPattern: Treating a volatile cache as the source of truth for financial integrity.

records.question: What should happen after an uncertain settlement response?
records.context: The external operation may have succeeded even when the response is missing. Compare safe investigation with an immediate retry.
records.source: Illustrative Bank Payment Journey decision question
records.assumptions: A status enquiry or reconciliation process can identify the original instruction.
records.risks: The external outcome may remain unknown beyond the proposed investigation target.

alternatives.title: Enquire and reconcile before replay
alternatives.summary: Retain pending state and the original reference. Establish the external outcome before deciding whether a replay is safe.
alternatives.benefits: Makes uncertainty explicit and avoids assuming that a timeout means failure.
alternatives.costs: Needs enquiry support, investigation ownership, and an exception path.
alternatives.consequences: Settlement hub coordinates investigation; Core ledger retains the posting reference; notification preserves pending semantics.
alternatives.antiPattern: Reporting success or failure without a definitive recorded outcome.

responsibilities.title: Payment API
responsibilities.purpose: Receives payment instructions, validates their shape, and assigns a traceable request reference. It coordinates the journey through downstream responsibilities.

responsibilities.title: Risk screening
responsibilities.purpose: Owns the decision to allow or hold a payment. It consumes risk signals and makes the decision explicit before ledger posting.

responsibilities.title: Core ledger
responsibilities.purpose: Owns the authoritative posting record. A repeated payment reference must not produce a second debit.

responsibilities.title: Settlement hub
responsibilities.purpose: Translates an internal payment into the external settlement contract. A delayed response needs status enquiry before any retry.

responsibilities.title: Notification service
responsibilities.purpose: Explains the payment outcome to the customer using the confirmed status. Notification failure does not reverse settlement.

groups.title: Control & accounting
groups.purpose: Risk decisions and authoritative financial records.

connections.label: Allow
connections.condition: Only an explicit allow decision permits posting.

options.title: pgBackRest for PostgreSQL
options.benefits: Full, differential and incremental backups with point-in-time recovery and verification.

options.title: Patroni high-availability manager
options.benefits: Automated leader election and failover for PostgreSQL, with fencing through a consensus store.
options.drawbacks: Failover moves the risk to split-brain and replication lag: both must be tested.

mappings.scope: Own workload execution and resource isolation; financial authority remains with the application.
Own durable state, unique references, and atomic updates. Do not imply ownership of an external core ledger.
Own durable delivery and redelivery semantics. The consumer still guards repeat financial effects.
Hold disposable derived values. Never use a cache-only check to authorise a financial effect.
Own routing, admission, and bounded connection behaviour; contracts remain with their producers.
Own authentication and entitlement decisions, credential lifecycle, and auditable denial.
Own correlated telemetry and alerts; financial records retain their authoritative owner.
Own recoverable copies and verification. A successful copy is not proof of a successful restore.
Own recovery sequencing, evidence, and authority to resume; do not infer that a timeout means failure.

threats.title: Payment without valid authority
threats.actor: Caller without authority for the instruction
threats.scenario: A caller submits or changes an instruction beyond the authority they hold.
threats.consequence: An unauthorised payment reaches downstream processing.
threats.priorityBasis: Illustrative payment risk judgement; confirm exposure and business impact.
threats.assumptions: Confirm actor capability, exposure, and existing protection.

threats.title: Repeated instruction changes the financial effect
threats.scenario: An original payment reference is replayed with changed business content or processed twice.
threats.consequence: Duplicate or inconsistent financial effects require investigation.
threats.priorityBasis: Illustrative payment risk judgement; confirm exposure and business impact.
threats.assumptions: Confirm actor capability, exposure, and existing protection.

threats.title: Sensitive data escapes its intended audience
threats.scenario: Instruction or settlement details appear in a support view, export, or log beyond the approved purpose.
threats.consequence: Confidential payment information becomes accessible outside its intended audience.
threats.priorityBasis: Illustrative payment risk judgement; confirm exposure and business impact.
threats.assumptions: Confirm actor capability, exposure, and existing protection.

threats.title: Payment activity cannot be reconstructed
threats.scenario: A decision, posting, or enquiry cannot be linked to its actor and original payment reference.
threats.consequence: Investigation cannot establish the accountable sequence of events.
threats.priorityBasis: Illustrative payment risk judgement; confirm exposure and business impact.
threats.assumptions: Confirm actor capability, exposure, and existing protection.
